Ours is public/core.json feats.rimesoul → resistances: [{type: 'cold', value: 'max(1,floor(@actor.level/2))'}]. The feat loop that reads it is src/rules/derive.ts:2307 inside deriveDefenses, and the same-type highest-wins pass at the end of that function is what makes their two-row form and our single max() form produce the same number at every level (L1 → 1, L4 → 2, L20 → 10). Compared value-by-value across levels, not just field presence. The second printed clause (environmental cold one step less severe) is modelled by neither side; ours records it as a note on the record.

public/core.json feats.steady-on-stone carries degreeShifts:[{shift:'successToCrit', skills:['acrobatics'], actions:['balance']}] and its own situational:[{targets:[skill acrobatics], …}]. degreeShifts is read at src/rules/explain.ts:309-320 (degreeShiftRecords) and the record-level situational at src/rules/explain.ts:475-486 (the `take` collector, feats walked there). Their row attaches the same sentence to the same skill with no value at all, so the player sees the same rule on the same stat; we additionally compute the shift.
